gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both entries identify the arbitrary-q loss construction as using unsigned signed powers for unrestricted-sign residuals, producing undefined or incorrect powers and an incorrect gradient weight instead of the signed duality map.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The loss and gradient must use |R|^q and |R|^{q-2}R for arbitrary q>1 and signed residuals; the printed [R]^q and [R]^{q-1} formulas do not establish the stated critical-point argument.

component_coverage.gold_component: The arbitrary-q residual loss and gradient use signed powers that are invalid or incorrect for unrestricted-sign residuals, so the critical-point proof is unsupported.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-002 explicitly identifies undefined noninteger powers, the mismatch with the norm power for odd integers, the false gradient formula, and the need for the signed weight |R_j|^{q-2}R_j.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-001 concerns deriving an inverse-norm bound from Gershgorin eigenvalue information, whereas the gold issue concerns transposing limiting Jacobians and incorrectly transferring row diagonal dominance to their transposes. It does not diagnose the missing regrouping as a transpose of a convex combination.

gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The numerical Hamiltonian does not implement the advertised normalized directional Hamiltonian: it omits the drift normalization and approximates sqrt(5) times the intended term.

component_coverage.gold_component: The implemented finite-difference Hamiltonian omits the 1/sqrt(5) drift normalization, thereby solving a different advection problem with propagation speed sqrt(5) rather than unit speed.
